title: Three equations, three unknowns
goal: Remove one letter at a time until one equation with one unknown stays.
generalHint: Remove the same letter from two pairs of equations. Then solve the two-unknown system. Check all three equations.

screens.label: RECALL
screens.title: Two unknowns again
screens.prompt: Solve the system. You use this method three times in this lesson.

answer.correctWhy: Add the rows: 2x = 6, so x = 3. Then y = 2.

mistakes.reply: Row 3 says 2x = 6. Divide both sides by 2. Then find y.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: Three numbers
screens.prompt: Three numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$ have the sum 6. Two more clues: $x - y + z = 2$ and $2x + y - z = 1$. Guess the numbers.
hints: Try small whole numbers. Check all three clues.
The numbers are 1, 2 and 3. Which one is x?
screens.caption: Type three guesses, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Remove x and z
screens.prompt: Subtract row 2 from row 1. The $x$ and $z$ terms cancel, so $2y = 4$. Find $y$.

answer.correctWhy: Row 4 says 2y = 4. Divide both sides by 2.

mistakes.reply: Row 4 says 2y = 4. Divide both sides by 2.

screens.tryTask: Tap row 1 and row 2. Then tap Subtract rows.
hints: Row 1 minus row 2: the x terms and the z terms are equal.
screens.caption: Subtract the rows, then type y.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Find x and z
screens.prompt: Add row 1 and row 3 to get $3x + 2y = 7$. Put in $y = 2$. Then find $x$ and $z$.

answer.correctWhy: Row 1 plus row 3: 3x + 2y = 7. With y = 2, x = 1. Then z = 6 − 1 − 2 = 3.

mistakes.reply: Check the order. Put x = 3, y = 2 and z = 1 into row 3. Is 2 · 3 + 2 − 1 equal to 1? Check all three equations.

screens.tryTask: Tap row 1 and row 3. Then tap Add rows.
hints: Row 1 plus row 3: the z terms cancel.
screens.caption: Type x, y and z.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: One letter at a time
screens.prompt: Remove the same letter from two pairs of equations. Then solve the two-unknown system. Check all three equations.

note.label: WORDS MATTER
note.text: A pair is two of the three equations. Make two pairs. Remove the same letter from each pair.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 2
screens.title: Two easy pairs
screens.prompt: Solve the system of three equations.

answer.correctWhy: Write x = y + 1 and z = y − 1. Then x + y + z = 3y = 9, so y = 3. So x = 4 and z = 2.

mistakes.reply: Put x = 2 and y = 3 into x − y = 1. Is it true? Check the order.

hints: Rows 2 and 3 link x and z to y.
Put x = y + 1 and z = y − 1 into row 1.

steps.text: Divide by 3. Then find x and z.

answer.correctWhy: 3y = 12, so y = 4. Then x = 5 and z = 3.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 2
screens.title: Remove the fraction
screens.prompt: Solve the system. First, multiply the first equation by 2 to remove the fraction.

answer.correctWhy: 2 · row 1: x + 2y = 4. Subtract row 3 from row 2: −y = −2, so y = 2. Then x = 0 and z = 3.

mistakes.reply: Multiply the full equation by 2. Then all coefficients are integers.

hints: Multiply row 1 by 2. Then no fraction is left.
Row 2 minus row 3 removes x and z.

steps.text: Multiply row 1 by 2. Multiply both sides.
Put y = 2 into x + 2y = 4. Then use row 3.

answer.correctWhy: 3 · row 1: x + 3y = 9. Row 2 minus row 3 gives −y = −2, so y = 2.

trap.question: True or false: remove x from one pair and y from the other pair. Then you can solve the two new equations.

options.label: True
options.reply: Each result still has two unknowns. Remove the same letter from both pairs.

feedback.correctWhy: Each new equation still has two unknowns. Remove the same letter from both pairs.
